Medicaid and long-term-care decisions often arrive at some of the most demanding moments in a family's life. A parent may suddenly need nursing-home care. A spouse may be trying to understand Long-Term Services & Supports. DSS may request financial records that span years. A family may be trying to keep a loved one safely at home while navigating HUSKY C, Medicaid waivers or other community-based supports.
Compass Title19 Consultants LLC exists to help Connecticut families bring clarity, organization and informed guidance to those moments.

We are a Connecticut-based, non-attorney Medicaid consulting and non-clinical care management organization focused on HUSKY C, Title 19, Medicaid LTSS, nursing-home Medicaid, applicable home and community-based services, applications, documentation, DSS verification requests, renewals and family care navigation.
Our purpose is simple: help families understand the process, prepare thoroughly, stay organized and know what comes next.

Why Compass Was Created
Compass was built around a reality that families encounter every day: Medicaid is more than an application.

Behind a single application may be years of financial records, changing care needs, multiple agencies, deadlines, verification requests, nursing-facility communication, family decisions and questions about what information DSS actually needs.

Families deserve more than a stack of forms and instructions. They deserve a knowledgeable guide who can help them understand the administrative process, organize what is required and recognize when another professional should be brought into the conversation.
That is the role Compass was created to fill.

We do not try to be everything to everyone. Our focus is Connecticut. Our core expertise is Connecticut Medicaid. And our work is grounded in careful preparation, professional boundaries and respect for the families who trust us during important transitions.
Meet Akua Achiaa Okyere, MBA
Founder & CEO
Akua Achiaa Okyere, MBA, is the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Compass Title19 Consultants LLC and a former Connecticut Department of Social Services eligibility professional.

Before founding Compass, Akua worked within Connecticut DSS, where her experience included Medicaid eligibility operations, complex case resolution, policy and procedure, staff development and training, quality assurance, cross-functional collaboration and the administration of public-benefit eligibility processes.

Her work included navigating detailed eligibility requirements, reviewing complex cases, supporting staff, resolving administrative issues and helping translate policy into consistent day-to-day eligibility operations.

That experience gave Akua a deep appreciation for both sides of the Medicaid process: the administrative standards agencies must follow and the very real difficulty families can experience when trying to satisfy those requirements during a healthcare or long-term-care transition.
Compass grew from the belief that this gap can be navigated better.
Experience With the System - Not Influence Over the System
Akua's former DSS experience is an important part of Compass's foundation, but it does not give Compass special access, preferential treatment or influence over Connecticut DSS.
Compass does not promise approvals, expedited decisions or particular outcomes.

Instead, Akua's background informs how Compass approaches a case: carefully reviewing the facts, organizing documentation, paying attention to notices and deadlines, anticipating administrative questions when reasonably possible, and helping clients communicate clearly and accurately.
Connecticut DSS and other applicable agencies remain solely responsible for Medicaid eligibility and benefit determinations.
Our value is preparation, experience and navigation - never special influence.
A Career Built Around Service, Analysis and Leadership

Akua's professional background extends beyond individual eligibility casework. Her experience includes leadership, employee training, performance management, complex problem solving, policy implementation, reporting and collaboration across teams and agencies.

She has recruited, trained and supported large groups of employees and has led teams responsible for high-volume public-benefit work. This combination of frontline eligibility knowledge and organizational leadership shapes the way Compass approaches client service today.
The result is a practice designed around systems: clear intake, careful document review, defined next steps, organized submissions, appropriate follow-up and professional accountability.
Education That Supports a Broader Perspective

Akua holds a Master of Business Administration in Management & Analytics from the University of Bridgeport and a bachelor's degree from the University of Ghana, Legon, with academic study in Psychology and Nursing.

Her combination of Medicaid eligibility experience, management and analytics education, and exposure to health and human-services disciplines supports Compass's practical approach to complicated family situations.

Compass is not a clinical healthcare practice, law firm, accounting firm or financial advisory firm. Akua's education and professional experience inform the company's consulting approach without replacing services that require separate professional licensure.
What Makes Compass Different?
We Focus on Connecticut Medicaid

Medicaid is administered within federal and state frameworks, and Connecticut has its own programs, terminology, administrative processes and eligibility structures. Compass deliberately focuses its Medicaid consulting services on Connecticut.
We Understand That Documentation Is Part of the Case

A family's eligibility circumstances matter, but so does the ability to document them. Compass places significant emphasis on organizing financial records, responding to verification requests, maintaining submission records and helping clients understand outstanding administrative requirements.
We Can Step Into a Process That Has Already Started

Not every client comes to Compass before applying. Families also contact us after an application has been submitted, after DSS requests additional verification, when an LTSS case is pending, or when the process has become difficult to manage.
When appropriate, Compass reviews what has already occurred before assuming the family needs to start over.
We Connect Medicaid Navigation With Non-Clinical Care Navigation

Long-term-care needs do not exist in separate boxes. A family may simultaneously be dealing with Medicaid, a nursing facility, home-care resources, a hospital transition, family communication and changing support needs.

Compass can provide non-clinical care management and family care navigation alongside Medicaid administrative assistance, while respecting the roles of licensed healthcare providers and official state-program care managers.
We Know When the Matter Belongs With Someone Else
A trustworthy consultant should know the boundaries of the work.

When a case involves legal interpretation, trusts, deeds, estate planning, significant transfers, legal asset-protection strategies, tax advice, investments, medical decisions or other matters outside Compass's scope, we encourage involvement of the appropriate qualified professional.
Compass values collaboration with elder-law attorneys, financial professionals, healthcare providers, nursing facilities, care managers and other professionals serving Connecticut families.

Clarify the process - explain the relevant administrative steps in understandable language.

Our objective is to help each client move through the administrative process with better information, stronger organization and a clearer understanding of the next step.

Connecticut Medicaid can become especially complicated when aging, disability or long-term care is involved. Families may encounter unfamiliar terms such as HUSKY C, Title 19, LTSS, spend-down, patient liability, community spouse, verification requests and home and community-based services.
This resource answers common questions in plain language and points families toward the part of the process that may require closer attention.
Medicaid rules are highly fact-specific and change over time. These answers are general education, not an individual eligibility determination.
Need Help With Your Connecticut Medicaid Situation? Schedule a Consultation
Understanding Connecticut Medicaid, Title 19 & HUSKY C
1. What is Title 19 in Connecticut?

Title XIX of the Social Security Act established the Medicaid program. In everyday Connecticut usage, people often say “Title 19” when referring to Medicaid, particularly in connection with long-term care. Connecticut administers Medicaid through HUSKY Health and other Medicaid program structures.
2. Is Title 19 the same thing as Medicaid?

Title XIX is the federal statutory authority for Medicaid. So “Title 19” is commonly used as another way of referring to Medicaid, although the specific Connecticut coverage group and eligibility rules still matter.
3. What is HUSKY C?

HUSKY C is Connecticut Medicaid coverage for eligible adults age 65 and older, adults who are blind or have disabilities, and certain working adults with disabilities. HUSKY C also includes Long-Term Services & Supports for qualifying individuals.
4. Is HUSKY C only for people in nursing homes?

No. HUSKY C includes medical coverage for eligible older adults and adults with disabilities and can also include LTSS. LTSS may be provided in a skilled nursing facility or through qualifying home and community-based services.
5. Does Compass handle every HUSKY program?

Compass's primary Medicaid practice focuses on Connecticut HUSKY C, LTSS, nursing-home Medicaid and applicable HCBS/waiver matters. Compass does not position itself as a HUSKY D-only termination or renewal service.
6. Can someone have both Medicare and Medicaid?

Yes. Some people qualify for both programs. Medicare and Medicaid have different eligibility rules and may cover different costs and services. Medicaid can cover services that Medicare generally does not, including qualifying long-term nursing-home and personal-care services.
Nursing Home Medicaid & Long-Term Care
7. Does Medicare pay for long-term nursing-home care?

Generally, no. Medicare may cover qualifying short-term skilled nursing facility care under specific conditions, but it does not generally pay for long-term custodial nursing-home care. Medicaid may help pay for long-term nursing-home care for people who meet Connecticut's financial and other eligibility requirements.
8. What is Connecticut Medicaid LTSS?

LTSS means Long-Term Services & Supports. Connecticut Medicaid LTSS can include skilled nursing-home care and qualifying home and community-based services for people who meet the applicable financial and level-of-care requirements.
9. When should a family start thinking about nursing-home Medicaid?

Ideally, before a financial or discharge crisis develops. Starting early gives a family time to understand the application process, locate records, review notices and determine whether legal, financial or other professional advice is needed.
10. How do I apply for Connecticut Medicaid LTSS?

Connecticut DSS provides an LTSS application process, including Form W-1LTSS and online resources through ConneCT. New LTSS applications are processed through designated LTSS Application Centers. The correct process depends on whether the person is seeking institutional or home/community-based LTSS.
11. Does DSS review five years of finances for nursing-home Medicaid?

In many LTSS cases, a five-year financial review is relevant. Connecticut DSS explains that HUSKY C LTSS may require a five-year income and asset review for individuals who have not previously received applicable DSS Medicaid benefits. The exact review depends on the person's Medicaid history and circumstances.
12. Why would DSS ask for years of bank statements?

Long-term-care Medicaid has financial eligibility and transfer rules. DSS may need financial records to evaluate assets, income, transactions and transfers during the applicable review period. A request for records does not by itself mean that the applicant did something wrong.
13. What happens if DSS sees a large withdrawal, transfer or deposit?

DSS may request documentation or an explanation to understand the transaction and determine whether it affects eligibility. The treatment depends on the facts. Transactions involving gifts, trusts, property, transfers or legal planning may warrant review by a qualified elder-law attorney.
14. Can Compass guarantee that nursing-home Medicaid will be approved?

No. Connecticut DSS determines Medicaid eligibility. Compass can help with preparation, documentation, verification requests and administrative navigation, but cannot guarantee approval, timing or a particular result.
Homes, Assets, Spouses & Financial Questions
15. Can I own a house and still qualify for Medicaid in Connecticut?

Possibly. Home ownership does not automatically prevent Medicaid eligibility. The treatment of a home depends on the Medicaid program, living circumstances, ownership, equity and other facts. Eligibility treatment and later estate-recovery questions are separate issues and should not be confused.
16. Does Medicaid automatically take my house when I apply?

No. Applying for Medicaid does not mean DSS simply takes ownership of a home. However, home ownership can raise eligibility, lien, estate-recovery and estate-planning questions depending on the circumstances. Because some of these are legal issues, Compass may recommend an elder-law attorney.
17. What happens when one spouse needs nursing-home care and the other stays home?

Medicaid includes special rules for married couples when one spouse requires institutional or certain long-term-care services and the other remains in the community. Connecticut refers to the spouse remaining in the community as the community spouse. Financial protections may apply, but the calculations and limits are program-specific and change over time.
18. Does the community spouse have to become impoverished for the other spouse to receive Medicaid?

Medicaid's spousal-impoverishment rules are intended to protect certain income and resources for the spouse remaining in the community. The amount that may be protected depends on current rules and the couple's circumstances.
19. Should I transfer my house or money to qualify for Medicaid?

Do not transfer assets simply because someone says it will help you qualify. Transfers can have Medicaid consequences, and property transfers may raise legal, tax and estate-planning issues. Compass does not provide legal asset-protection advice and may recommend consultation with an elder-law attorney before significant transfers.
20. What is a Medicaid transfer penalty?

Certain transfers for less than fair market value during an applicable LTSS review period may affect Medicaid payment for long-term-care services. Whether a transfer is penalized, exempt or otherwise treated differently depends on the facts and governing rules. Legal questions should be reviewed by an attorney.
21. What is patient liability?

For certain LTSS recipients, patient liability is the portion of a recipient's income that must be contributed toward the cost of care after applicable deductions. Connecticut DSS calculates the amount based on program rules and individual circumstances.
Spend-Down & HUSKY C Financial Eligibility
22. What is a HUSKY C Medicaid spend-down?

Some people who otherwise meet HUSKY C requirements but have income above the applicable limit may qualify through a medical spend-down. Qualifying medical expenses can be used toward the spend-down amount. The rules depend on the coverage group and current DSS standards.
23. Does 'spend-down' mean I have to spend all my money?

Not necessarily. The term can be confusing. A HUSKY C medical spend-down generally concerns qualifying medical expenses in relation to income eligibility. Asset/resource eligibility is a separate issue and should be analyzed under the applicable Medicaid category.
24. Where can I find current Medicaid income and asset limits?

Because Medicaid financial standards can change, use current Connecticut DSS program standards rather than relying on an older article or social-media post. Compass also avoids embedding changing dollar amounts into evergreen website pages unless the page is dated and regularly updated.
Home & Community-Based Services
25. Can Medicaid help someone remain at home instead of entering a nursing home?

Potentially. Connecticut offers home and community-based services through several Medicaid and state program pathways. Eligibility can involve financial criteria, functional or level-of-care assessments and program-specific requirements.
26. What does HCBS mean?
HCBS means Home and Community-Based Services. These services are intended to support eligible people in home or community settings rather than relying exclusively on institutional care.
27. What is a Medicaid waiver?

A Medicaid waiver allows a state, with federal approval, to provide certain services or use program rules that differ from the standard Medicaid State Plan. Connecticut operates multiple HCBS waiver programs for different populations.
28. Does everyone who qualifies financially automatically receive a Medicaid waiver?

No. Financial eligibility is only one part of many HCBS programs. Functional eligibility, level-of-care criteria, program-specific requirements, assessments and sometimes program capacity can also matter.
29. Can Compass determine whether I am clinically eligible for a waiver?

No. Compass can help with Medicaid eligibility administration, documentation and navigation within its scope, but it does not perform state clinical or functional eligibility determinations and cannot guarantee waiver enrollment or service authorization.
30. Is Compass a home-care agency?
No. Compass is not a home-care agency and does not supply aides, homemakers, companions, CNAs or nurses. Compass provides Medicaid consulting and non-clinical care management/family care navigation.
Applications, DSS Verification & Pending Cases
31. What documents might DSS ask for during a Medicaid application?

The exact documents depend on the program and case. DSS may request proof of income, assets, financial accounts, deductions, insurance, property, marital information or other facts relevant to eligibility. LTSS cases can require more extensive financial documentation.
32. What is a DSS verification request?

It is a request for documents or other proof DSS needs to evaluate information relevant to eligibility. The applicant should read the entire notice, pay attention to deadlines and respond with accurate information.
33. What if I do not have the exact document DSS requested?

Connecticut DSS's verification guidance recognizes that different forms of proof may sometimes be available. If you do not have a listed form of verification, contact the assigned worker about what other proof may be acceptable. DSS ultimately decides whether the verification is sufficient.
34. Can Compass help if I already filed my Medicaid application?
Yes, depending on the case. Compass can review an existing or pending application, DSS notices and available documentation and determine what administrative assistance it can provide.
35. Do I have to start a new Medicaid application if my current one seems stuck?

Not necessarily. “Stalled” is not an official DSS status, and a case may still be pending or awaiting information. Before filing a duplicate application, it is generally sensible to determine what happened with the existing case.
36. Can Compass communicate with DSS for me?

When appropriate authorization is in place and the service is included in the engagement, Compass may assist with administrative communication and follow-up. Compass does not have special access to DSS or authority over DSS decisions.
37. What if DSS denied my Medicaid application?

Review the entire notice immediately because deadlines and rights may apply. Compass can review administrative documentation within its scope, but if the matter requires legal advice, an appeal or hearing representation, Compass may recommend a qualified attorney.
Renewals & Redeterminations
38. Do I have to renew Medicaid after I am approved?

Medicaid eligibility is reviewed periodically. The timing and requirements depend on the coverage group and current rules. Recipients should respond to DSS renewal notices and keep contact information current.
39. How can Connecticut Medicaid recipients manage renewals?

Connecticut DSS provides online benefits-management options including MyDSS and ConneCT/MyAccount. DSS states that clients can use MyDSS to check benefit status, report changes, renew benefits and upload documents.
40. What if DSS asks for more information after I submit my renewal?
The renewal may remain incomplete until DSS receives and reviews needed verification. Compass can help organize the administrative request and responsive documentation within its scope.
41. Can Compass help if I did not use Compass for my original application?
Yes. Compass can assist with qualifying existing applications, verification requests and renewals even when another person or organization handled the original application.
42. What if my Medicaid coverage stopped after a renewal?

First identify the reason stated in the DSS notice. The appropriate response may differ depending on whether the issue involves missing information, eligibility changes, an incomplete renewal or another reason. Legal appeal issues may require an attorney.
Working With Compass
43. Is Compass Title19 Consultants LLC a law firm?
No. Compass is a Connecticut-based, non-attorney Medicaid consulting and non-clinical care management organization.
44. Do I need an attorney to apply for Connecticut Medicaid LTSS?

Connecticut DSS states that an attorney is not required to complete an LTSS application. However, legal advice may be valuable when a case involves trusts, property transfers, estate planning, legal rights or other legal issues. Compass and elder-law attorneys can serve different, complementary roles.
45. What can Compass do that is different from an elder-law attorney?

Compass focuses on Medicaid administrative navigation: application preparation, document organization, DSS verification requests, existing applications, renewals and related non-clinical care navigation. Attorneys provide legal advice and representation. Some families benefit from both services.
46. What kinds of cases does Compass focus on?

Compass focuses primarily on Connecticut HUSKY C, Title 19, nursing-home Medicaid, LTSS, applicable HCBS/waiver matters, Medicaid documentation, verification requests, existing applications, renewals and non-clinical care navigation.
47. Who founded Compass?

Compass was founded by Akua Achiaa Okyere, MBA, a former Connecticut Department of Social Services eligibility professional whose experience included Medicaid eligibility operations, complex case resolution, policy and procedure, staff training and quality assurance.
48. Does Akua's former DSS employment give Compass special influence with DSS?

No. Compass has no special access, authority or influence over DSS decisions. That prior experience informs Compass's understanding of Connecticut Medicaid administration and its approach to preparation and documentation.
49. Does Compass guarantee Medicaid approval?
No. No consultant can properly guarantee a Connecticut DSS eligibility determination. Compass helps clients prepare, organize and navigate the process; DSS determines eligibility and benefits.
50. Does Compass serve all of Connecticut?
Yes. Compass Title19 Consultants LLC is based in Hartford and serves clients throughout Connecticut.

Compass can review the situation, identify the administrative issues within our scope and help the family understand the next steps.

You may be helping a parent enter a nursing home. You may be trying to keep a loved one safely at home. Schedule a Connecticut Medicaid Consultation
What Is Title 19 in Connecticut?

Title XIX of the Social Security Act established Medicaid. Medicaid is jointly funded by the federal government and states, while individual states administer their Medicaid programs within federal requirements.
In Connecticut, Medicaid coverage is provided through several HUSKY Health categories.
HUSKY A — Medicaid for certain children, parents, caretaker relatives and pregnant individuals.
HUSKY B — Connecticut's Children's Health Insurance Program.
HUSKY C — Medicaid for adults age 65 and older and adults with disabilities, including Long-Term Services & Supports.
HUSKY D — Medicaid for certain low-income adults without dependent children.
Compass's consulting practice focuses primarily on HUSKY C, Medicaid LTSS and related long-term-care needs, rather than every HUSKY category.

Why Can a Connecticut Title 19 Application Become Complicated?
Submitting an application may only be the beginning.

Depending on the Medicaid program and the applicant's circumstances, DSS may need information concerning income, assets, financial accounts, property, insurance policies and other eligibility factors.

Long-term-care Medicaid can involve particularly extensive financial review. For certain applicants, Connecticut's LTSS eligibility process may include review of prior financial activity and transfers.

Families may therefore find themselves gathering and organizing substantial documentation while simultaneously dealing with hospitalization, declining health, a nursing-home admission or caregiving responsibilities.
This is where Compass can help bring organization and direction to the administrative process.
Connecticut Nursing Home Medicaid & LTSS

Connecticut Medicaid's Long-Term Services & Supports programs can provide coverage for eligible individuals requiring ongoing care, including certain skilled nursing facility and home- and community-based services.
Eligibility is not based on age alone. Depending on the program, DSS may consider financial and non-financial requirements, and additional functional or program-specific criteria may apply.

Compass assists clients with the administrative Medicaid eligibility and application process, including helping families understand documentation requirements and organize information requested by DSS.

Frequently Asked Questions About Connecticut Title 19
Is Title 19 the same as Medicaid?
Title XIX of the Social Security Act is the federal statutory authority for Medicaid. In everyday conversation, people sometimes use “Title 19” and “Medicaid” interchangeably.
Is HUSKY C the same as Title 19?
HUSKY C is one category of Connecticut Medicaid. It serves certain adults age 65 and older and adults with disabilities and includes Long-Term Services & Supports.
Does Title 19 pay for nursing-home care in Connecticut?
Medicaid LTSS may provide skilled nursing facility coverage for individuals who satisfy applicable eligibility requirements. Connecticut DSS makes the eligibility determination.
Do I have to be completely out of money before applying?

Medicaid eligibility is considerably more nuanced than simply having “no money.” Financial requirements vary depending on the Medicaid coverage group and individual circumstances. Do not dispose of or transfer assets simply because you believe you need to qualify for Medicaid; transfers can have significant eligibility and legal consequences.
Does Connecticut review previous financial activity for long-term-care Medicaid?
For certain LTSS applicants, Connecticut Medicaid eligibility may involve review of prior financial activity and transfers. The applicable review depends on the program and circumstances.
Can I own a home and receive Title 19?

Property treatment depends on the Medicaid program and individual circumstances. Home ownership does not automatically answer whether someone is eligible. Because property can also raise estate-recovery and legal-planning considerations, obtain individualized professional advice before transferring, selling or changing ownership of property.
Can Compass determine whether DSS will approve me?

No. Only the appropriate government agency can determine Medicaid eligibility and approve an application. Compass helps clients understand and navigate the application and administrative process but cannot guarantee Medicaid eligibility or approval.
Do I need an attorney to submit a Medicaid application?

Not necessarily. However, trusts, asset transfers, estate planning, property ownership, appeals and other legal issues may require advice from a qualified attorney. Compass will recommend legal counsel when an issue falls outside our non-attorney scope.
Can Compass take over an application I've already started?

Depending on the circumstances, yes. We can review the status of an existing application and determine whether Compass can assist with outstanding documentation, verification requests and administrative follow-up.

No. Compass serves clients throughout Connecticut. Our office is located in Hartford.

renewals.title: Keep Your Connecticut Medicaid Coverage on Track

blocks.text: Receiving Medicaid is not always the end of the eligibility process. Connecticut DSS may periodically review whether a person remains eligible and may request updated information, a completed renewal, or additional verification.

A renewal can become stressful when the household has experienced changes, financial records are difficult to gather, the recipient receives Long-Term Services & Supports (LTSS), or a DSS deadline is approaching.

Compass Title19 Consultants LLC helps Connecticut individuals, seniors, adults with disabilities, families and caregivers navigate Medicaid renewals and redeterminations within our non-attorney scope.
Our focus includes HUSKY C, Medicaid LTSS, nursing-home Medicaid and applicable home- and community-based Medicaid coverage.
Schedule a Connecticut Medicaid Renewal Consultation
What Is a Medicaid Renewal or Redetermination?
A Medicaid renewal or redetermination is the process used to review whether a current Medicaid recipient continues to meet applicable eligibility requirements.
DSS may review information such as income, assets, household circumstances and other program-specific factors. The exact requirements depend on the Medicaid coverage group.
A renewal should not be treated as routine paperwork that can safely be ignored. If DSS needs information and does not receive it, coverage may be affected.
How Do Connecticut Medicaid Recipients Renew Benefits?

Connecticut DSS currently provides MyDSS as a mobile-friendly way for existing clients to manage benefits. DSS states that clients can use MyDSS to check benefit status, report changes, renew benefits and upload documents.
DSS also provides MyAccount through ConneCT for online benefits management.
The correct renewal process can depend on the program and the notice received. Follow the instructions and deadline contained in the recipient's current DSS notice.
Need Help Understanding Your Renewal Notice? →
What Information Might DSS Request?
The information required depends on the recipient's Medicaid category and circumstances.
Depending on the case, DSS may request updated information or verification concerning:
Income, including Social Security, pensions, wages or other income
Bank and financial accounts
Assets or resources when applicable to the coverage group
Health insurance or Medicare information
Household or marital circumstances
Address or residency information
Medical expenses when relevant
Life insurance or other resources when applicable
Long-term-care circumstances
Other information needed to determine continued eligibility
DSS's online renewal process may generate a Verification Checklist showing documents needed based on the information reported during the renewal.
Compass can help clients organize the documentation relevant to their renewal and respond to administrative verification requests within our scope.
HUSKY C Renewals
HUSKY C serves eligible older adults, adults who are blind or have disabilities, certain working adults with disabilities, and individuals receiving applicable Long-Term Services & Supports.
Because HUSKY C includes coverage groups with financial eligibility requirements, a renewal may involve updated income, asset or other eligibility documentation depending on the recipient's category.
Compass focuses on HUSKY C and can assist clients with understanding renewal notices, organizing requested documentation and administrative follow-up.
Get Help With a HUSKY C Renewal →
LTSS and Nursing Home Medicaid Renewals
Individuals receiving Medicaid Long-Term Services & Supports may also be subject to ongoing eligibility reviews.
For LTSS recipients, changes involving income, assets, marital circumstances, property or other eligibility factors can require careful attention.

Connecticut DSS distinguishes new LTSS applications from renewals and interim changes. New applications are handled through LTSS Application Centers, while renewals and interim changes continue through the statewide ConneCT model.
Compass can assist with the administrative renewal process, documentation organization and applicable DSS requests.
Get Help With an LTSS Medicaid Renewal →
What If Something Changed Since the Last Eligibility Review?
A renewal is an opportunity to provide current and accurate information.
Depending on the program and circumstances, relevant changes may include:
A change in income
Opening or closing a financial account
A change in marital status
A move or change of address
A change in household composition
Changes in insurance or Medicare coverage
Changes involving assets or property
Admission to or discharge from a nursing facility
Changes in long-term-care services
Other changes affecting eligibility
Connecticut DSS also allows clients to report changes and upload supporting verification through its online benefits-management tools.
Do not conceal, alter or misrepresent information in an attempt to preserve Medicaid eligibility. Information submitted to DSS should be accurate and complete.
Received a DSS Renewal Notice?
Read the Entire Notice and Pay Attention to the Deadline.
DSS notices contain important information about what the recipient must do, what documents may be needed and when information is due.
If you receive a renewal packet or request:
Read every page
Identify the due date
Review prefilled information for accuracy
Note changes that need to be reported
Gather requested documentation
Keep copies of what you submit
Follow the submission instructions in the notice
Watch for additional DSS correspondence after submission
If the notice is confusing, Compass can review the administrative correspondence with you and help identify the next steps within our scope.
Schedule a DSS Renewal Notice Review →
What If DSS Requests Additional Verification?
Submitting the renewal does not always complete the process.
DSS may request additional information or documentation before it can determine continued eligibility.
Compass can help:
Review the administrative verification request
Identify the requested documents
Organize available records
Identify missing items
Prepare an organized documentation package
Maintain a record of what was submitted
Assist with appropriate administrative follow-up when authorized
Provide Compass with the complete DSS notice, including all pages and attachments.
What If I Already Submitted My Renewal?
If you have already submitted a renewal but are uncertain about its status, do not automatically submit another renewal without understanding what happened to the first one.
Connecticut DSS advises clients who have submitted renewals to use their online account to view current case status. MyDSS also allows clients to check benefit status.
Compass may be able to review the available documentation and assist with appropriate administrative follow-up.
Ask Compass to Review a Pending Renewal →
What If My Medicaid Benefits Stopped?
The first step is to determine why coverage ended.
DSS may issue notices explaining the reason for a change or termination and any available next steps.
If the issue involves a missed or incomplete renewal, outstanding verification or another administrative matter, Compass can review the documents and determine what assistance falls within our scope.
If the matter involves an appeal, hearing, legal interpretation or other legal issue, Compass may recommend consultation with an appropriate attorney.
Do not assume that every termination can be resolved in the same way. The correct response depends on the reason stated by DSS and the recipient's circumstances.
How Compass Helps With Medicaid Renewals
Renewal Notice Review
We help clients understand what an administrative renewal notice is requesting and identify important deadlines.
Renewal Documentation Organization
We assist clients in gathering and organizing information relevant to the renewal.
HUSKY C Renewal Support
We provide administrative renewal assistance for applicable HUSKY C cases.
LTSS Renewal Support
We assist with Medicaid LTSS renewal documentation and related administrative requirements within our scope.
DSS Verification Requests
We help clients organize documentation requested after a renewal is submitted.
Reported Changes
We help clients understand how a reported change may fit into the administrative Medicaid process and organize supporting information.
Pending Renewal Follow-Up
When appropriately authorized, Compass may assist with administrative follow-up concerning a pending renewal.
Professional Collaboration
When the matter raises legal, tax, investment, financial or other licensed-professional issues, Compass encourages the client to consult the appropriate professional.
Get Help With Your Connecticut Medicaid Renewal →
Don't Wait Until the Due Date
Some documents can take time to obtain.
Bank records, pension information, insurance documentation and other verifications may not be immediately available.
Starting early provides time to review the renewal, identify missing information and respond to unexpected requests.
If you have received a renewal notice and believe you may need assistance, contact Compass before the deadline whenever possible.
Why Choose Compass?
Connecticut Medicaid Is Our Focus
Compass Title19 Consultants LLC was founded by Akua Achiaa Okyere, MBA, a former Connecticut Department of Social Services eligibility professional.
Her DSS experience included Medicaid eligibility work, complex case resolution, policy and procedure, staff training, quality assurance and eligibility operations.
Compass brings that Connecticut-specific experience to families navigating HUSKY C, LTSS and related Medicaid administrative processes.
We Help Organize Complicated Documentation
Renewals can involve multiple records, notices and verification requirements. We help bring structure to the process.

Important Note About Changing Medicaid Rules
Medicaid rules and renewal procedures can change.

Connecticut DSS is currently implementing federally required HUSKY Health changes with different effective dates. For example, DSS states that HUSKY D renewal frequency will change to every six months beginning January 1, 2027.
Compass's primary practice focus is HUSKY C, LTSS and related long-term-care Medicaid services, not HUSKY D-only matters.
For this reason, clients should rely on their current DSS notice and current program rules rather than older online information.
Compass reviews current administrative guidance applicable to the services within our scope.
Frequently Asked Questions About Connecticut Medicaid Renewals
What is a Medicaid redetermination?
It is an eligibility review used to determine whether a current Medicaid recipient continues to qualify under the applicable program rules.
How do I know when my Medicaid renewal is due?
DSS sends renewal information and notices. Review the due date shown on your current notice and keep your contact information current so important correspondence reaches you.
Can I renew Connecticut Medicaid online?
DSS provides online benefits-management tools, including MyDSS and MyAccount through ConneCT, that allow eligible clients to renew benefits and upload documents.
What happens if I miss my renewal deadline?
Coverage may be affected. The appropriate next step depends on the case and DSS notice. Review the notice promptly and seek assistance if needed.
What documents will I need?
Requirements vary by Medicaid coverage group and circumstances. DSS may request income, asset, insurance, household, medical-expense or other verification.
Can Compass help with my HUSKY C renewal?
Yes. HUSKY C renewal and redetermination assistance is within Compass's primary Medicaid focus, subject to the individual case and engagement.
Can Compass help with nursing-home Medicaid or LTSS renewals?
Yes. Compass can assist with administrative LTSS renewal documentation and related DSS requests within our scope.
What if DSS asks for more documents after I renew?
Compass can review the administrative request and help organize responsive documentation.
Can Compass help if I did not use you for my original Medicaid application?
Yes. We can review an existing renewal or redetermination even if Compass did not prepare the original application.
Can Compass guarantee that my Medicaid will continue?
No. Connecticut DSS determines continued Medicaid eligibility. Compass cannot guarantee a particular eligibility outcome.
Can Compass represent me at an appeal or hearing?
Compass is a non-attorney organization. If a matter requires legal representation or legal advice regarding an appeal or hearing, we may recommend an appropriate attorney.
Does Compass handle HUSKY D renewals?
Compass's primary practice focus is HUSKY C, LTSS and related long-term-care Medicaid matters. We do not position Compass as a HUSKY D-only termination or renewal service.
Protect the Coverage You've Worked to Establish
A Medicaid renewal can look simple until documents, changes and verification requests begin to accumulate.

Whether you are renewing HUSKY C, maintaining LTSS coverage for a loved one, responding to DSS or trying to understand why a renewal remains pending, Compass can help you navigate the administrative process with greater organization and clarity.

waivers.title: Helping Connecticut Residents Explore Long-Term Care at Home and in the Community

blocks.text: Needing long-term care does not always mean moving into a nursing home.

Connecticut offers Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) that can help eligible older adults and people with disabilities receive long-term services and supports while living at home or in another community setting.

Compass Title19 Consultants LLC helps Connecticut individuals, families and caregivers understand the Medicaid eligibility and administrative process connected with certain HCBS and waiver programs. We assist with Medicaid applications, financial documentation, DSS verification requests, renewals, existing applications and related administrative navigation within our scope of services.
Schedule a Connecticut HCBS & Medicaid Waiver Consultation
What Are Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS)?

Home and Community-Based Services, commonly called HCBS, are long-term services and supports provided outside an institutional setting. Connecticut offers multiple community-based programs to help eligible people remain at home or return to community living.

Depending on the program and the individual’s assessed needs, community-based supports may include personal care, assistance with activities of daily living, care management, respite, habilitative supports, home-based services and other approved supports.
Not every HCBS program is the same, and not every program is a Medicaid waiver. Connecticut uses a combination of Medicaid State Plan services and waiver programs.
Talk With Compass About Community-Based Care →
What Is a Medicaid Waiver?

A Medicaid waiver allows a state, with federal approval, to operate certain Medicaid services or eligibility arrangements differently from the standard Medicaid State Plan. In Connecticut, several long-term-care programs use Medicaid waiver authority to provide services in home and community settings.

A waiver is not simply a general exemption from Medicaid rules. Each program has its own target population, functional requirements, financial requirements, covered services and administrative process.
Being interested in a waiver does not automatically establish eligibility. The appropriate state agency determines whether an applicant meets the requirements for a particular program.
Who Might Benefit From HCBS?
Families often explore HCBS when an individual:
Needs help with bathing, dressing, eating, mobility, medication routines or other daily activities
Wants to remain at home rather than enter a nursing facility
Has a disability and needs ongoing supports in the community
Is preparing to transition from an institutional setting back into the community
Needs personal-care or attendant support
Has an acquired brain injury and may need specialized community supports
Is an older adult at risk of nursing-home placement
Has received a DSS request for financial documentation connected with an LTSS application
Has already started a waiver or HCBS Medicaid application and needs help with the administrative process
The right program depends on age, disability, level of care, financial eligibility, living arrangement, assessed needs and other program-specific requirements.
Connecticut Has More Than One HCBS Program

Connecticut offers several community-based programs, and different state agencies may administer or operate different services. This is why families should not assume that “the Medicaid waiver” refers to one single program.

Programs relevant to older adults and adults with disabilities can include the Connecticut Home Care Program for Elders (CHCPE), Acquired Brain Injury waiver services, Personal Care Assistance-related supports, Katie Beckett coverage, Community First Choice and other programs administered through Connecticut agencies. Programs operated by the Department of Developmental Services also serve eligible individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities.

Program rules, availability and enrollment processes can change. Compass helps clients understand the Medicaid administrative side of the process and, when appropriate, identify the agency or professional that handles other parts of the program.
Connecticut Home Care Program for Elders (CHCPE)
The Connecticut Home Care Program for Elders helps eligible older adults receive services in the community rather than entering or remaining in a nursing facility.

Connecticut DSS describes the program as serving eligible Connecticut residents age 65 and older who are at risk of nursing-home placement and who meet applicable program requirements. CHCPE includes different service and funding categories, including Medicaid-supported components for qualifying individuals.

Because financial and functional standards can change, Compass recommends reviewing the current requirements applicable at the time assistance is sought rather than relying on an older online dollar limit.
Ask Compass About CHCPE Medicaid Eligibility →
Acquired Brain Injury (ABI) Waiver Services
Connecticut operates Medicaid waiver services for certain individuals with acquired brain injuries who meet program-specific requirements and can be supported in the community.

ABI cases can involve both program eligibility and Medicaid financial eligibility. Compass can assist with the Medicaid application, financial documentation and DSS administrative requirements within our scope, while clinical, functional and programmatic determinations remain with the appropriate state agencies and professionals.
Personal Care and Self-Directed Supports

Some Connecticut community-based programs allow eligible participants to receive personal-care or attendant supports and, in certain programs, exercise greater direction over how approved services are delivered.

Community First Choice (CFC), for example, has provided eligible individuals living in the community access to personal attendant care and other supports through a self-directed model. Connecticut has also been evaluating changes affecting how certain CFC participants receive services, so current program guidance should be checked when applying or planning services.

Compass does not determine functional eligibility, allocate service hours or guarantee access to a particular program. We can assist with Medicaid eligibility documentation and administrative navigation when those services fall within our engagement.
HCBS and HUSKY C
For many older adults and adults with disabilities seeking long-term services and supports, Medicaid financial eligibility is connected with HUSKY C and LTSS requirements.
HCBS applicants may therefore encounter both a program or functional assessment and a Medicaid financial eligibility review. These are related but distinct parts of the process.
A person may satisfy one part of the process while additional information is still needed for another.
Learn About Connecticut HUSKY C Medicaid →
How Do I Apply for Medicaid HCBS in Connecticut?

The application route depends on the program. For Medicaid LTSS home- and community-based waiver applications, Connecticut DSS currently directs new statewide HCBS Medicaid applications to the Greater Hartford LTSS Application Center. The W-1LTSS is the state application used for Long-Term Services and Supports.
Some community programs also have their own referral, screening or functional-assessment process in addition to Medicaid financial eligibility.

Submitting a form is therefore not always the entire application process. Applicants may need to complete assessments and provide financial and non-financial verification before eligibility and services can be determined.
Financial Eligibility for Medicaid Waiver Services
Medicaid-funded HCBS programs can have financial eligibility requirements involving income, assets and other factors. The applicable rules depend on the coverage group and waiver program.

For certain LTSS applicants, DSS may conduct an extensive financial review, including review of prior financial activity. The documentation required can differ based on the applicant’s Medicaid history and circumstances.
What Documents Might Be Needed?
Depending on the Medicaid program and applicant, DSS may request documentation involving:
Identity and Connecticut residency
Social Security and other income
Pensions and retirement income
Checking and savings accounts
Investment or retirement accounts
Life insurance
Property or other resources
Medicare and other health coverage
Financial transactions or transfers when applicable
Other information needed to determine Medicaid eligibility
The program responsible for functional eligibility may separately request medical, clinical or care-needs information.
How Compass Helps With HCBS & Medicaid Waiver Cases
Medicaid Eligibility Navigation
We help clients understand the Medicaid administrative requirements associated with qualifying long-term-care programs.
Application Preparation
We assist with organizing the information and documentation needed for the Medicaid portion of an LTSS or waiver application.
Financial Documentation Organization
We help clients gather and organize financial records and identify documentation that may still be outstanding.
DSS Verification Requests
If DSS requests additional information, we help clients understand the administrative request, organize responsive documentation and prepare for appropriate follow-up within our scope.
Existing Applications
If an HCBS Medicaid application has already been started, Compass can review the administrative status and determine whether we can assist with outstanding Medicaid documentation and DSS follow-up.
Renewals & Redeterminations
We can assist clients with organizing Medicaid documentation requested during renewal or redetermination.
Care Navigation

When appropriate within our care-management services, Compass can help families understand the different organizations involved and identify next steps, while recognizing that program assessments and service authorization belong to the responsible agencies.
Get Help Navigating an HCBS Medicaid Application →
Already Applied and the Process Has Stalled?
HCBS applications can involve more than one organization, which can make it difficult for families to know where a case stands.

You may have completed a functional assessment but still have a Medicaid eligibility issue. DSS may be waiting for financial verification. A family member may have submitted documents but not know what remains outstanding. Or an application may have been started months ago and no one is certain about the next step.
Compass can review the Medicaid administrative side of an existing case and determine whether we can assist with outstanding documentation, verification requests, authorization and follow-up.
You may not need to start the entire process over simply because you need help now.
Ask Compass to Review an Existing HCBS Medicaid Case →
What If DSS Sends a Verification Request?
Read the entire notice and pay close attention to any response deadline.
DSS verification requests may ask for bank records, income verification, explanations, property information or other documentation needed to determine Medicaid eligibility.
Compass can help clients organize the administrative response and maintain a clear record of information submitted within the scope of our engagement.
Schedule a DSS Verification Review →
Can HCBS Prevent Nursing Home Placement?

For some eligible individuals, community-based services can make it possible to receive needed long-term supports outside a nursing facility. Programs such as CHCPE are specifically designed to help qualifying older adults remain in community settings when their needs can be appropriately supported there.
However, HCBS is not appropriate or immediately available in every situation. Functional needs, safety, program criteria, service availability and financial eligibility all matter.
Compass does not promise that a particular person can avoid nursing-home placement or that a particular waiver will be approved.
Compare Home-Based Care and Nursing Home Medicaid Options →
Are Medicaid Waiver Services Automatically Available Once I Qualify for Medicaid?
No. Medicaid financial eligibility and eligibility for a particular HCBS program are not necessarily the same thing.

A waiver or community program may have additional functional, clinical, age, disability, level-of-care or program-specific requirements. Some programs may also have capacity or enrollment considerations.
The responsible state agency or program makes those determinations.
Do I Need an Attorney for an HCBS Medicaid Application?
Not necessarily. Many Medicaid applications can be completed without an attorney.

Compass provides non-attorney Medicaid application, documentation and administrative support. However, legal advice may be appropriate when a case involves trusts, significant asset transfers, estate planning, property ownership, legal interpretation, appeals or other legal issues.
When a matter falls outside our scope, Compass encourages clients to work with an appropriate Connecticut elder-law attorney or other licensed professional.
Why Choose Compass for Connecticut HCBS Medicaid Guidance?
Connecticut Medicaid Experience

Compass Title19 Consultants LLC was founded by Akua Achiaa Okyere, MBA, a former Connecticut Department of Social Services eligibility professional. Her DSS experience included Medicaid eligibility work, complex case resolution, policy and procedure, staff training, quality assurance and eligibility operations.
Compass applies that Connecticut-focused experience to help individuals and families navigate Medicaid administrative requirements with greater clarity and organization.
Connecticut-Focused Practice
We focus on Connecticut Medicaid and long-term-care programs rather than trying to navigate the different Medicaid systems of multiple states.
Individualized Guidance
We review the circumstances of the individual case rather than assuming every waiver applicant has the same needs.
Documentation Support
We help clients organize the financial and administrative documentation that can become one of the most difficult parts of Medicaid eligibility.
Clear Professional Boundaries
We distinguish Medicaid administrative assistance from legal, clinical and financial advice and collaborate with appropriate professionals when needed.
Support for Existing Cases
Families can contact Compass even after an application has already been started.
Compass Is a Non-Attorney Medicaid Consulting & Care Management Organization
Compass Title19 Consultants LLC is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice.

We assist with Medicaid education, application preparation, documentation, administrative navigation, DSS verification requests, renewals and related care-management services within our professional scope.
We do not determine clinical or functional eligibility for HCBS programs, control waiver enrollment, allocate services or guarantee Medicaid or waiver approval.
When legal, tax, investment, financial, clinical or other licensed professional advice is required, clients should consult the appropriate professional.
Frequently Asked Questions About Connecticut Medicaid Waivers & HCBS
What does HCBS mean?
HCBS means Home and Community-Based Services. These are long-term services and supports delivered in home or community settings rather than an institutional setting.
Is every home-care program a Medicaid waiver?
No. Connecticut uses both Medicaid State Plan services and waiver programs. The correct program depends on the individual’s circumstances.
Can Medicaid pay for care at home in Connecticut?
For eligible individuals, Medicaid-funded programs may cover certain home and community-based long-term services and supports. Eligibility and covered services vary by program.
What is CHCPE?
The Connecticut Home Care Program for Elders helps qualifying adults age 65 and older who are at risk of nursing-home placement receive eligible services in the community.
Is Community First Choice a Medicaid waiver?

Community First Choice has operated as a Medicaid State Plan service rather than a traditional 1915(c) waiver. Connecticut has been considering changes to how certain participants receive services, so current DSS guidance should be checked.
Do I need HUSKY C for a Medicaid waiver?
Many LTSS waiver applicants are evaluated under Medicaid financial eligibility rules associated with HUSKY C, but the exact pathway depends on the program and individual circumstances.
Does qualifying financially guarantee waiver services?
No. A particular HCBS program can have additional functional, clinical, age, disability or level-of-care requirements. The responsible agency makes program eligibility and service determinations.
Can Compass help me choose the right waiver?

Compass can help you understand the Medicaid and care-navigation landscape and identify appropriate next steps within our scope. Final program eligibility and service determinations are made by the responsible state agencies.
Can Compass help if I already started an HCBS application?
Yes, depending on the circumstances. We can review the Medicaid administrative status and determine whether we can assist with outstanding documentation, DSS requests and follow-up.
Does Compass guarantee waiver approval?
No. Compass cannot guarantee Medicaid eligibility, waiver enrollment, service authorization, processing time or approval.
Does Compass serve all of Connecticut?
Yes. Compass serves individuals and families throughout Connecticut from our Hartford office.

blocks.text: Caring for an aging parent, spouse or adult with disabilities often involves much more than completing a Medicaid application. Families may be coordinating providers, appointments, home-care services, benefits, paperwork, facility communication and changing care needs—all at the same time.

Compass Title19 Consultants LLC provides non-clinical care management and family care navigation to help Connecticut families organize those moving parts, understand available resources and maintain a clearer path forward.

Our care management services can complement our Connecticut Medicaid expertise, particularly when a family is navigating HUSKY C, Long-Term Services & Supports (LTSS), nursing-home care or home and community-based services (HCBS).
Schedule a Care Management Consultation
Important: Compass Is Not a Home-Care Agency

Compass provides consulting, administrative coordination, resource navigation and family support. We do not send aides, companions, homemakers, CNAs, nurses or other direct-care workers into clients’ homes, and we do not provide hands-on care.
What Care Management Means at Compass

At Compass, non-clinical care management is a consulting and navigation service designed to help individuals and families understand needs, organize information, connect with appropriate resources and keep track of important next steps. Compass is not a home-care agency and does not employ or dispatch caregivers to provide hands-on care in a client’s home.

Depending on the engagement, Compass may help a family identify priorities, coordinate administrative information among involved parties, locate community resources, prepare for care transitions, organize benefit-related documentation and maintain a practical care-navigation plan.

Compass does not provide hands-on personal care, homemaker or companion services, home-health services, medical care, nursing assessments, therapy, emergency services, or state-program care management. When those services are needed, Compass helps families identify and coordinate with the appropriate provider or agency.
Who May Benefit From Care Management?
Older adults who want to remain safely in the community
Families coordinating care for an aging parent
Adults with disabilities and their caregivers
Families navigating a transition from hospital or rehabilitation to home
Families considering home care, assisted living or nursing-home options
Individuals applying for or receiving Medicaid LTSS or HCBS
Long-distance family caregivers who need a Connecticut-based point of coordination
Families overwhelmed by multiple providers, agencies, notices and appointments
Individuals whose care needs or living situation are changing
How Compass Can Help
Care Needs & Priority Organization
We help families identify the practical issues requiring attention and organize a manageable list of priorities and next steps.
Family Care Navigation
We help families understand the care landscape, identify appropriate resources and determine which agency, provider or professional may need to be contacted.
Medicaid & Benefits Coordination

Home & Community Resource Navigation

Care Transition Support

Transitions from a hospital, rehabilitation setting, nursing facility or home can involve many administrative details. Compass can help families organize the non-clinical pieces and identify resources that may be needed.
Provider & Professional Coordination
With appropriate permission, Compass can help families organize communication among relevant providers and professionals, while recognizing each professional's independent role and scope.
Document & Information Organization
We help families create order around notices, benefit documents, provider information, care-related records and administrative follow-up.
Ongoing Family Support
For engagements that include ongoing support, Compass can help families track changing needs, outstanding tasks and administrative issues over time.
Care Management and Connecticut Medicaid
Long-term care and Medicaid often intersect.

Connecticut DSS describes LTSS as care provided at home, in community-based settings or in facilities such as nursing homes. Connecticut also offers multiple HCBS options designed to help eligible individuals receive supports at home or return to community living.
For families who need both care navigation and Medicaid assistance, Compass can help connect the administrative pieces so that the family is not treating each issue as an unrelated problem.
For example, a family may need help understanding a Medicaid verification request while also coordinating home-care resources and preparing for a change in living arrangements.
Compass can provide continuity across those non-clinical administrative needs.
Care Management vs. State-Program Care Management
It is important to distinguish Compass's private care-management/navigation service from care management that may be assigned or authorized through a Connecticut Medicaid or state program.

For example, Connecticut's Home Care Program for Elders (CHCPE) includes care management among its available services. In applicable state programs, designated access-agency or program care managers may conduct assessments, develop or monitor formal plans of care, authorize or coordinate covered services, or perform other functions assigned by the state.
Compass does not replace a DSS-designated, access-agency, DDS, DMHAS, health-plan or other official program care manager.

Instead, Compass can help the client and family stay organized, understand the broader process, manage Medicaid-related administrative responsibilities within our scope and coordinate with official program personnel when appropriate and authorized.
Care Management and HCBS

Connecticut offers a variety of home and community-based services to help eligible individuals live at home or in community settings. Some programs operate through Medicaid waivers, while others operate under the Medicaid State Plan or state-funded structures.

Exploring home and community-based supports
Moving into assisted living
Entering a nursing facility

Experiencing a significant change in support needs

Medication administration or medical management
Psychotherapy or mental-health treatment
Emergency response or 24-hour crisis coverage
Legal advice or legal representation
Tax, investment or financial advice
Guarantees of Medicaid eligibility or approval

Her DSS experience included Medicaid eligibility work, complex case resolution, policy and procedure, staff training, quality assurance and eligibility operations.
